Objectives of the intervention are to strengthen the right to freedom of expression, to enable people to exercise their cultural rights especially the right to artistic creativity, to express, share and discuss in the public sphere diverse narratives and perspectives on Cambodia's social, political and cultural contexts and to explore the potential of civic participation via the arts in Cambodia.

Syftet med insatsen är att stärka rätten till yttrandefrihet, göra det möjligt för människor att utöva sina kulturella rättigheter, särskilt rätten till konstnärlig kreativitet, att uttrycka, dela och diskutera olika berättelser och perspektiv på Kambodjas sociala, politiska och kulturella sammanhang i den offentliga sfären och att utforska potentialen för medborgardeltagande via konsten i Kambodja.

title.narrative: Agreement on Cambodia Living Arts, Culture, Democracy and Human Rights
Decision on contribution on Cambodia Living Arts, Culture, Democracy and Human Rights

description.narrative:
Below are key results in 2023.
Stand for Culture Fellows are inspired to engage in policy forums: Stand for Culture Fellows is one of CLA's activities under the Civic Participation through the Arts programme that was carried out in 2022. It is a pilot study focusing on policy and advocacy work. Through the independent review commissioned by CLA in 2023, this activity is proved to be one of the smart strategies in strengthening and engaging civil society in policy making decision due to its well designed curriculumn that is well fit to the context of Cultural and Creative Industries (CCI) workers, leaders and artist's nature, many of whom fear involving in policy dialogue, discussion and lobby/advocacy. The review also revealed that there is potential and capacity in CCI workers in advocacy and lobbying as long as they are equipped with skills to better prepare them in engaging in policy dialogue and decision making. A result from this activity was that one of the 6 recommendations presented by the fellows during a dialogue with Ministry of Tourism was accepted in integrating the arts programs during the SEA Game last year hosted by Cambodia. With this achievement, the fellows start to see the importance of the dialogue/lobby with the government in order to enhance the arts sector.
CLA used the cultural season as a platform to engage with youth. In 2023, CLA successfully transformed itself from being an implementer to a facilitator as the whole cultural season was fully produced and managed by CLAs programme fellows. The theme of 2023 cultural season Your kind, our kind delved into relationship between individuality, societal norms and pressures and how it affects expression and creativity. The season provided an opportunity for emerging artists to present their new creation relevant to the set themes including voice from underrepresented community. As part of the season, the team also organized a panel discussion on urbanization and heritage/identity where stories, experiences from the voice of artists, writers, thinkers as well as youth were shared and discussed. The season has reached 125,000 people in Phnom Penh and 4 provinces consisted of 12 communities.
The youth-led festival is another experimental project deriving from finding and recommendation of research conducted in 2020 seeking to understand the potential of involving youth in the arts to foster civic participation in Cambodia. In 2023, the 7 color festival was carried out by the 4 interns with no prior arts experience, but passionated in arts, under the theme 'Linkage' which was subdivided into three categories -¨Youth and Yesterday¨, ¨Youth and Today¨ and ¨Youth and the future¨. It involves dialogue across diversity, promoted volunteering and collective ownership, and provide avenues for self-expression. It also addressed issues such as gender equality, LGBTQ rights and social justice forstering meaning discussions and shared experiences.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
